summary.headline: Max India Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to INR72 crores and quarterly loss narrowed to INR6.8 crores from INR35.5 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR213.4 crores, up 30% from INR164 crores, and the EBITDA loss narrowed to INR83 crores from INR99 crores. Q4 revenue was INR72 crores, up 45% QoQ and 58% YoY, with the consolidated loss at INR6.8 crores versus INR27.8 crores in Q3. Management said the Noida Phase 1 partial occupancy certificate unlocks receivables of over INR150 crores and allows re-filing for Phase 2. Care homes and AGEasy both grew sharply, though care home occupancy averaged lower due to new beds added in Q4. Management is still seeking a fundraise, timing dependent on market conditions.

financial_highlights.change: +45% QoQ (vs INR49.8 crores in Q3); +58% YoY (vs INR45.5 crores in Q4 FY25)
vs INR27.8 crores in Q3 FY26 and INR35.5 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR11.4 crores in Q4; INR38.8 crores in FY26
INR23 crores in Q4; about INR77 crores in FY26

segments.name: Residences (Dehradun)
segments.commentary: Fully occupied and consistently profitable; FY26 revenue INR24.2 crores and profit INR2.3 crores, including about INR1.7 crores marketing fee from 5 resale releases.

segments.name: Residences (Gurgaon Estate 360 / 361)
segments.commentary: Estate 360 fully sold with ITD collections of INR534 crores at 87% efficiency; management fee earned INR45.6 crores till Mar-26 (INR26 crores in FY26). Estate 361 Phase 1 (180 units) has 127 bookings at March-end and 141 sold as of date, with INR69 crores collected in April-May.

segments.name: Antara Assisted Care (care homes and care at home)
segments.commentary: 485 beds across 8 care homes in NCR, Bengaluru and Chennai; 3,400 patients served in Q4. Occupancy on mature beds rose (Sector 41 26% to 34%, Noida 13% to 38%, Bannerghatta 10% to 37%), and Noida contribution margin improved from -19% to +6% QoQ.

segments.name: AGEasy (D2C and marketplace wellness)
segments.commentary: Q4 net revenue INR23 crores; March-26 RoAS exit at 2.9 vs 1.8 for the year; online gross margin improved from 38% to 46%. Holds 3 granted patents and 3 filed; NPS 45.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the consolidated loss to improve further in FY27, with one or two verticals showing path to profitability in the later part of FY27.
AGEasy targeted for EBITDA breakeven by the last quarter of FY27; monthly exit revenue run rate of INR14-16 crores for FY27 indicated.
Antara Assisted Care consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected around H1 FY28; care home unit-level contribution breakeven takes 4-6 quarters.
Noida Phase 2 re-approval and sales start expected during FY27, with launch hoped by end of 2026.
Estate 361 Phase 2 (remaining 180 units) launch announcement expected within days; company commits to 1.5 million sq ft in the project.
Management fee estimates: E360 about INR130 crores lifetime, E361 about INR200 crores lifetime, Noida Phase 1 about INR14 crores pending possession-linked payments.
capex_capacity: Care homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; 28 beds in one Gurgaon home under renovation, expected live soon; 5 of 7 mature homes tracking to the model, per management.
Care home target economics: ROCE of 25-26%, 32%+ contribution margin and 16-18% EBITDA margin at maturity; 50-bed home takes 8-10 quarters to reach 65-70% occupancy.
New bed additions to be explored in H2 FY27, with site search starting around October-November 2026 (6-9 months lead time).
Noida Phase 1: partial occupancy certificate received for 3 towers by ContendBuilders SPV; construction complete, about INR70-75 crores of pending finishing bills.
Noida Phase 2: about 440,000 sq ft (about 220 units) yet to be developed; re-approval of revised building plans required before sales.

Pipeline: Sector 105 Noida intergenerational project (1.1 million sq ft), 2 further opportunities (Bangalore and Dehradun); management says all three could total about 2 million sq ft. Chandigarh project lost height clearance post Operation Sindoor.
demand_pricing: Estate 361 Phase 1 sold 141 of 180 units by the call date; management said inventory is nearly exhausted for certain unit types.
Noida Phase 2 market pricing is 2-3x Phase 1 realisations, at about INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft per management, implying roughly INR700 crores-plus potential on the 440,000 sq ft remaining.
AGEasy RoAS: marketplaces about 1.0 at start of FY26, exit about 2.0; D2C from 0.7-0.8 to 1.7-1.8. Online gross margin 38% to 46%; 65% of 19 FY26 launches at 50%+ gross margin.

AGEasy COGS pressure from China sourcing (30% of sourcing) due to geopolitics; mitigated by alternate Indian vendors, larger pre-orders and small price increases. No significant margin impact in Q3 or Q4 per management.
Care home occupancy averaged lower because of new homes added in Q4; mature beds grew about 10% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: When will Estate 361 Phase 2 launch, and are residential collections lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 launch announcement expected within days as 140 of 180 units are sold; collections are lumpy, with booking fee of INR25 lakh, then 10% on application and another 10%, with construction-linked collections over about 3 quarters, lumpy in FY27 and more regular from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the management fee outlook for E360, E361 and Noida, and the direct cost?
qa_highlights.answer: E360 about INR130 crores and E361 about INR200 crores lifetime management fee; Noida about INR14 crores pending. Variable cost is about 15% of fee; post-completion annuity is about INR10-12 crores per 250-unit community (60% CAM, 40% discretionary).

qa_highlights.question: Will Noida Phase 2 start and how much is pending on Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 sales expected during FY27 after re-approval of building plans; about 440,000 sq ft remaining. Phase 1 construction complete, with INR70-75 crores of pending bills to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: Why no entry into Hyderabad and what is the status of partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Residence entry delayed by unlimited FSI which lets developers maximise density; assisted living in Hyderabad is on the list and to be examined later in FY27. boAt watch product has not taken off as expected, but tech solutions are being worked on; IIT partnership on wheelchairs is a major revenue contributor.

qa_highlights.question: Is AGEasy on track for INR500 crores revenue around FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects continued high growth year-on-year, similar to the past two years, without reiterating the INR500 crore target numerically.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn EBITDA and PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to show path to profitability for one or two verticals in later FY27; labour code and minimum wage revisions are a watch item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of new labour codes and staff costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code impact is about INR3-4 crores across entities, mainly gratuity provisioning, recognised in FY27 as the code came in March 2026. Payroll is about INR80-90 crores; management said the reported top line excludes SPV sales.

qa_highlights.question: When is the fundraise and what about the INR32 crore tax demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Fundraise timing depends on market sentiment; cash comfortable for 3-6 months, with an update expected this year. The INR32 crore tax demand on Dehradun is being contested via rectification for unallowed brought-forward losses; if accepted, it reduces to nil.

risks_watch: Lumpy residential collections: FY27 expected to be lumpy, with EBITDA losses possible in some periods despite overall project profitability.
Funding: company cash cover quoted as 3-6 months; equity raise timing tied to market conditions and not yet executed.
Noida Phase 2 approvals are pending; Phase 1 SPV profitability reduced by cost escalation and only net profit is consolidated.
Care home occupancy on new beds and the 2H FY27 bed expansion plan; unit-level breakeven still 4-6 quarters away.
Input cost risk for AGEasy from China sourcing and geopolitics; minimum wage revisions and labour code impact on costs.
INR32 crore income tax demand on Dehradun pending rectification outcome.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the Noida approval, but cautious on profitability timing: the chairman avoided hard EBITDA and PAT dates, citing geopolitics and wage revisions. Management was candid on lumpy collections, occupancy dilution from new homes and the fundraise delay.
key_quotes: We expect these numbers to further improve in the coming financial year. This will be a testimony to our commitment to demonstrate path to profitability in all our businesses.

This event also has a potential to unlock the receivables of upwards of INR150 crores and also gives us an opportunity now to re-file for approval of Phase 2, which also is a big unlock given the way the market has now matured, the price points are 2x, 3x of what we sold last time.
While the average occupancy has shown a decline, it is only because of the addition of new care homes in last quarter FY26.
So difficult for me to make a forward-looking statement, but the intention is to demonstrate that during this year.
